title: Ganpati Infrastructure Development Company Limited v. State of U.P. & 4 Others
coram: Rajesh Bindal, C.J. and J.J. Munir, J.
disposition: Writ petition dismissed as withdrawn; Clause 4.9 vires not decided
headnote: A developer's writ, objected to as covering the same ground as its pending Writ Petition No. 40192 of 2018 challenging the 13th Amendment to the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and seeking a declaration that Clause 4.9 Part A and Part-B are ultra vires, was connected with that petition and later listed with leading Writ-C No. 4545 of 2019. Maintainability of the second writ was not decided. On Civil Misc. Withdrawal Application No. 2 of 2022 the petition was dismissed as withdrawn. Clause 4.9 and the amendment were not construed.
facts:
Ganpati Infrastructure Development Company Limited filed Writ-C No. 3235 of 2019 against the State of U.P. and four others. On 29 January 2019 counsel for a respondent objected that the same petitioner had already filed Writ Petition No. 40192 of 2018, still pending, challenging the 13th Amendment to the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005 and seeking to declare Clause 4.9 Part A and Part-B ultra vires, and that a second writ seeking more or less the same relief was not maintainable. The affidavit was of Ranjan Srivastava, the same deponent as in the earlier writ. Petitioner's counsel sought time to verify.

The petition was later connected with Writ Petition No. 40192 of 2018, with leave to file a counter, and then listed with leading Writ-C No. 4545 of 2019, whose order of date was to be seen. On 12 May 2022 Rajesh Bindal, C.J. and J.J. Munir, J. allowed Civil Misc. Withdrawal Application No. 2 of 2022 and dismissed the petition as withdrawn.

holding_units.topic: vires challenge to Clause 4.9 / 13th Amendment connected with pending similar writs and later withdrawn
holding_units.question: Is Clause 4.9 Part A and Part-B of the U.P. Electricity Supply Code, 2005, as substituted by the 13th Amendment, ultra vires, and is a second writ on that point maintainable while the petitioner's earlier writ remains pending?
holding_units.holding: Not decided. Counsel for a respondent objected that the petitioner's Writ Petition No. 40192 of 2018, challenging the 13th Amendment and seeking to declare Clause 4.9 Part A and Part-B ultra vires, was still pending, and that a second writ seeking more or less the same relief was not maintainable. The Court listed the matter, later connected it with that petition, and then listed it with leading Writ-C No. 4545 of 2019, whose order of date was to be seen. On Withdrawal Application No. 2 of 2022 the petition was dismissed as withdrawn. Neither maintainability nor the vires of Clause 4.9 was decided.
